description: Config-driven ACL discovery (D-64, Recommendation A; issue #74). Each case describes the acl.root config value plus the filesystem state at the resolved path; `expected` captures whether an ACL is attached to the Executor and whether enforcement is therefore active. CRITICAL INVARIANT: a missing acl.root path attaches NO ACL (acl_attached=false) and MUST NOT synthesize an empty default-deny ACL — even when acl.default_effect is 'deny' — otherwise every inter-module call in a project with no ACL would be silently denied. acl.root is a directory by convention; the loaded file is <root>/global_acl.yaml (PROTOCOL_SPEC §3.1 `acl/{scope}_acl.yaml`), but acl.root MAY point directly at a YAML file. acl.root defaults to './acl' in all three SDKs (Rust no longer hard-requires it). Auto-discovery is skipped when the caller supplies their own Executor, so an explicitly-wired ACL is never clobbered. acl.root is resolved relative to the config file's directory when the Config knows its source path, else relative to CWD. The rule-evaluation semantics of a loaded ACL are covered by acl_evaluation.json; this fixture covers only the discovery/attachment behavior.

test_cases.comment: Rust previously hard-required acl.root and rejected omission with CONFIG_INVALID; under D-64 omission is valid and the default applies (parity with Python/TS).
acl.root may point directly at a YAML file instead of a directory.
Resolved path does not exist -> no ACL attached, no enforcement.
Directory exists but contains no global_acl.yaml -> still a no-op.
The D-64 non-breaking invariant: default_effect=deny in config must NOT produce a deny-everything ACL when the path is missing.
When the caller passes their own Executor, auto-discovery is skipped so an explicitly-wired ACL is never overwritten.
